## formal
Let $\Cl(p,q)$, $n = p + q \ge 1$, have orthonormal generators $e_{1}, \dots, e_{n}$, with $Q(e_{i}) = +1$ for $i \le p$ and $Q(e_{i}) = -1$ for $i$ in $N = \{p + 1, \dots, n\}$, and for $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ let $e_{S}$ be the increasing product of the $e_{i}$, $i \in S$. Identify the subsets with $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}$, addition being the symmetric difference $S \triangle T$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The sign from symmetry.)} Let $x_{1}, \dots, x_{n}$, $n \ge 2$, be elements of an algebra over a field $k$ with $x_{i}x_{j} = c\,x_{j}x_{i}$ for all $i \ne j$, for one $c \in k$, and $x_{1}x_{2} \ne 0$. Then $c^{2} = 1$. Moreover, if only the single relation $x_{1}x_{2} = c\,x_{2}x_{1}$ is imposed ($c \ne 0$), then $x_{1}^{2}x_{2} = c^{2}x_{2}x_{1}^{2}$, so wherever $x_{2}x_{1}^{2} \ne 0$ the square $x_{1}^{2}$ commutes with $x_{2}$ exactly when $c^{2} = 1$. Over a field of characteristic other than $2$, with $c \ne 1$ this gives $c = -1$: the symmetry of the relation and the centrality of the squares each force $c \in \{1, -1\}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The quadratic form.)} $e_{S}^{2} = (-1)^{q(S)}$ with $q(S) = \binom{|S|}{2} + |S \cap N| \bmod 2$, and $e_{S}e_{T} = \pm e_{S \triangle T}$. The map $q : \mathbb{F}_{2}^{n} \to \mathbb{F}_{2}$ is a quadratic form whose polar form
\[
b(S,T) = q(S \triangle T) + q(S) + q(T) = |S|\,|T| + |S \cap T| \bmod 2
\]
is $1$ exactly when $e_{S}$ and $e_{T}$ anticommute. So the group $\{\pm e_{S}\}$ is a central extension of $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}$ by $\{\pm 1\}$ with commutator form $b$ and squaring map $q$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The radical.)} The radical of $b$ is $\{\emptyset\}$ for $n$ even and $\{\emptyset, \{1, \dots, n\}\}$ for $n$ odd, and $q(\{1, \dots, n\}) = 1$ exactly when the pseudoscalar squares to $-1$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The Gauss sum and the type.)} For any $j$ with $j^{2} = -1$ (a unit bivector of a Euclidean plane, say),
\[
\sum_{S} e_{S}^{2} \;=\; \sum_{S}(-1)^{q(S)} \;=\; \big\langle (1 - j)(1 + j)^{p}(1 - j)^{q} \big\rangle_{0},
\]
and its value is $2^{n/2}$ for $p - q \equiv 0, 2$, $-2^{n/2}$ for $p - q \equiv 4, 6$, $2^{(n+1)/2}$ for $p - q \equiv 1$, $-2^{(n+1)/2}$ for $p - q \equiv 5$ and $0$ for $p - q \equiv 3, 7 \pmod 8$. Define the Arf invariant of a quadratic form $q'$ with nondegenerate polar form on $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{m}$ by $\sum (-1)^{q'} = (-1)^{\mathrm{Arf}(q')}\,2^{m/2}$. For $n$ even, $\mathrm{Arf}(q) = 0$ exactly when $\Cl(p,q)$ is a real matrix algebra ($p - q \equiv 0, 2 \bmod 8$) and $\mathrm{Arf}(q) = 1$ exactly when it is a quaternionic one ($p - q \equiv 4, 6$). For $n$ odd, $q$ is nonzero on the radical exactly in the complex case ($p - q \equiv 3, 7$); otherwise $q$ descends to the quotient by the radical, whose Arf invariant is $0$ for a sum of two real matrix algebras ($p - q \equiv 1$) and $1$ for a sum of two quaternionic ones ($p - q \equiv 5$). So the parity of $n$, the value of $q$ on the radical and the Arf invariant determine the type in the classification.
\item[(v)] \emph{(The ascent.)} Add one hyperbolic plane spanned by $e, f$ with $Q(e) = 1$, $Q(f) = -1$, put $\omega = ef$, and take the twisted generators $x_{i}\omega$ of the commuting-copies isomorphism (Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}). For $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ and $B \subseteq \{e, f\}$ the product of the $x_{i}\omega$, $i \in A$, with the blade $e_{B}$ is $\pm$ a blade of $\Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1)$, and $(A, B) \mapsto$ its index set is a linear bijection $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n} \oplus \mathbb{F}_{2}^{2} \to \mathbb{F}_{2}^{n+2}$ carrying $q_{(p,q)} \perp q_{(1,1)}$ to $q_{(p+1,q+1)}$. The form $q_{(1,1)}$ has Arf invariant $0$, so the $(1,1)$ ascent leaves the Gauss sum's sign, the Arf invariant and the type unchanged (the division-ring clause of Theorem \claimref{tower.rigidity-clock-frozen}); the anisotropic plane $(0,2)$, whose Clifford algebra is the quaternions, has $q = 1$ on its three nonzero elements and Arf invariant $1$; adding it is not an orthogonal sum with the ground form, since the twist by its volume element, of square $-1$, exchanges $p$ and $q$: $\Cl(p, q{+}2)$ carries $q_{(q,p)} \perp q_{(0,2)}$.
\end{enumerate}

## technical
The signs of the squares of the basis blades of a real Clifford algebra form a quadratic form over the two-element field: index the blades by subsets of the generators, so that multiplying blades adds their index sets by symmetric difference, and record a $1$ when the blade squares to $-1$. The associated bilinear form records exactly which pairs of blades anticommute, so the finite group of signed blades is the central extension that this form describes. The form's own invariants recover the classification. In even dimension the anticommutation form is nondegenerate and the Arf invariant, read off from the sign of the Gauss sum $\sum_{S} e_{S}^{2}$, is $0$ for the real matrix algebras ($p - q \equiv 0, 2 \bmod 8$) and $1$ for the quaternionic ones ($p - q \equiv 4, 6$). In odd dimension the radical is spanned by the pseudoscalar: if it squares to $-1$ the algebra is complex, and otherwise the Arf invariant of the quotient separates two real from two quaternionic matrix algebras. The Gauss sum is the scalar part of $(1 - j)(1 + j)^{p}(1 - j)^{q}$ with $j^{2} = -1$, which gives the whole table at once.

Two small structural facts sit underneath. A single commutation coefficient shared by all pairs of directions must satisfy $c^{2} = 1$, because the relation must read the same with the two directions exchanged; and, with only one relation imposed, the same condition $c^{2} = 1$ is what makes the square of a direction central. Either way $c \in \{1, -1\}$, and $c = -1$ needs the separate input $c \ne 1$. These are classical: the classification by the quadratic form is in Ovsienko and in Elduque and Rodrigo-Escudero, and is restated here. In the language of the series, adding a hyperbolic plane, the $(1,1)$ increment of the transport ascent, adds an orthogonal summand of Arf invariant $0$ once the ground generators are twisted by the plane's volume element, so the type never changes up the tower, while the anisotropic plane $(0,2)$, whose algebra is the quaternions, carries Arf invariant $1$; adding it is not an orthogonal sum with the ground form, since the twist by its volume element, of square $-1$, exchanges $p$ and $q$: $\Cl(p, q{+}2)$ carries $q_{(q,p)} \perp q_{(0,2)}$.

## lay
Every product of basic directions in these algebras squares either to plus one or to minus one. Writing down which ones give minus one produces a simple yes-or-no table, and that table already knows which kind of number system the whole algebra is built on: ordinary real numbers, complex numbers or quaternions. Adding a pair of directions of opposite type, the basic step the series uses to repair division, never changes that answer; adding two directions that both square to minus one is different, because it also swaps the roles of the existing positive and negative directions.

## one-liner
The signs $e_{S}^{2} = (-1)^{q(S)}$ of the blades of $\Cl(p,q)$ form a quadratic form over $\mathbb{F}_{2}$ whose polar form is anticommutation; its Gauss sum $\sum_{S} e_{S}^{2} = \langle (1 - j)(1 + j)^{p}(1 - j)^{q}\rangle_{0}$, the value of $q$ on the radical and its Arf invariant give the real, complex or quaternionic type, and the $(1,1)$ ascent adds a summand of Arf invariant $0$.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{(i)} Exchanging $i$ and $j$ in the relation gives $x_{j}x_{i} = c\,x_{i}x_{j}$, so $x_{1}x_{2} = c\,x_{2}x_{1} = c^{2}x_{1}x_{2}$ and $(1 - c^{2})x_{1}x_{2} = 0$; since $x_{1}x_{2} \ne 0$ and $c$ is a scalar of a field, $c^{2} = 1$. With only the relation $x_{1}x_{2} = c\,x_{2}x_{1}$, moving $x_{2}$ through $x_{1}x_{1}$ uses it twice: $x_{1}^{2}x_{2} = c\,x_{1}x_{2}x_{1} = c^{2}x_{2}x_{1}^{2}$, so $x_{1}^{2}x_{2} - x_{2}x_{1}^{2} = (c^{2} - 1)x_{2}x_{1}^{2}$, which vanishes, when $x_{2}x_{1}^{2} \ne 0$, exactly when $c^{2} = 1$. In characteristic other than $2$, $c^{2} = 1$ and $c \ne 1$ give $c = -1$. The check verifies the second statement in the normal-ordered model of the algebra with one relation $x_{2}x_{1} = c^{-1}x_{1}x_{2}$ for $c = 2, \tfrac13, -1, 1$ (the square $x_{1}^{2}$ is central exactly for $c = \pm 1$, and these are exactly the values for which the relation reads the same both ways), and in $\Cl(p,q)$ that distinct generators anticommute and every $e_{i}^{2}$ is central.

\emph{(ii)} By Proposition \claimref{std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute}, $e_{S}e_{T} = \pm \prod_{i \in S \cap T} Q(e_{i})\, e_{S \triangle T} = \pm e_{S \triangle T}$, the generators having squares $\pm 1$. Reversing the $k = |S|$ letters of $e_{S}$ costs $\binom{k}{2}$ transpositions, and $e_{S}\widetilde{e_{S}} = \prod_{i \in S}Q(e_{i}) = (-1)^{|S \cap N|}$, so $e_{S}^{2} = (-1)^{\binom{k}{2}}e_{S}\widetilde{e_{S}} = (-1)^{q(S)}$. Moving $e_{T}$ past $e_{S}$ letter by letter gives $e_{S}e_{T} = (-1)^{b(S,T)}e_{T}e_{S}$ with $b(S,T) = |S|\,|T| + |S \cap T|$ (each letter of $T$ passes the $|S|$ letters of $S$, anticommuting with all but the one equal to it, if any). Then $e_{S \triangle T}^{2} = (e_{S}e_{T})^{2} = e_{S}e_{T}e_{S}e_{T} = (-1)^{b(S,T)}e_{S}^{2}e_{T}^{2}$, which is $q(S \triangle T) = q(S) + q(T) + b(S,T)$. The form $b$ is bilinear over $\mathbb{F}_{2}$, since $|S \triangle S'| \equiv |S| + |S'|$ and $|(S \triangle S') \cap T| \equiv |S \cap T| + |S' \cap T| \bmod 2$, and $q(\emptyset) = 0$; so $q$ is a quadratic form with polar form $b$. The group $\{\pm e_{S}\}$ maps onto $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n}$ with kernel $\{\pm 1\}$, central; its commutators are $(-1)^{b}$ and its squares $(-1)^{q}$. The check compares the GA products with the closed forms for every pair of blades in all twenty signatures with $n \le 5$.

\emph{(iii)} $S$ lies in the radical when $b(S, \{i\}) = |S| + [i \in S] = 0$ for every $i$. If $S$ is neither empty nor everything, taking $i \in S$ and $i' \notin S$ gives $|S| \equiv 1$ and $|S| \equiv 0$; $S = \emptyset$ always lies in the radical, and $S = \{1, \dots, n\}$ does exactly when $n \equiv 1 \bmod 2$. Its square is the pseudoscalar's, whose sign is that of Proposition \claimref{primer.sign}.

\emph{(iv)} For $k \ge 0$, $(-1)^{\binom{k}{2}} = \langle (1 - j)j^{k}\rangle_{0}$ (the values for $k = 0, 1, 2, 3$ are $1, 1, -1, -1$, and both sides have period $4$ in $k$). Grouping the subsets by $a = |S \setminus N|$ and $b' = |S \cap N|$,
\[
\sum_{S}(-1)^{q(S)} = \Big\langle (1 - j)\sum_{a, b'}\binom{p}{a}\binom{q}{b'}j^{a}(-j)^{b'}\Big\rangle_{0} = \big\langle (1 - j)(1 + j)^{p}(1 - j)^{q}\big\rangle_{0},
\]
all products taken in the commutative algebra $\mathrm{span}\{1, j\}$. There $(1 + j)(1 - j) = 2$, $(1 + j)^{2} = 2j$, $(1 + j)^{8} = 16$, so with $r = p - q \ge 0$ the product is $2^{q}(1 - j)(1 + j)^{r}$, and $\langle (1 - j)(1 + j)^{s}\rangle_{0} = 1, 2, 2, 0, -4, -8, -8, 0$ for $s = 0, \dots, 7$; with $r = 8m + s$ and $n = r + 2q$ this is the stated table. For $r < 0$ the product is $2^{p}(1 - j)^{|r| + 1}$, and the automorphism $j \mapsto -j$ of $\mathrm{span}\{1, j\}$ turns its scalar part into that of $2^{p}(1 + j)^{|r| + 1}$; since $\langle (1 + j)^{t}\rangle_{0} = 1, 1, 0, -2, -4, -4, 0, 8$ for $t = 0, \dots, 7$, and $(1 + j)^{8} = 16$, so that for $|r| + 1 \ge 8$ the value is $16^{m}$ times the tabulated one, the same table follows. For $n$ even the polar form is nondegenerate by (iii) and the definition of the Arf invariant applies directly; comparing the sign of the Gauss sum with the classification (Theorem \claimref{transport.classification-real-clifford-algebras}: $p - q \equiv 0, 2$ real, $4, 6$ quaternionic, $1$ two real, $5$ two quaternionic, $3, 7$ complex matrix algebras) gives the even statement. For $n$ odd with $q(\{1, \dots, n\}) = 1$, $S \mapsto S \triangle \{1, \dots, n\}$ changes $q$ by $1$ (since $b(S, \{1, \dots, n\}) = 0$), so the Gauss sum is $0$ and by (iii) the pseudoscalar squares to $-1$, the complex case $p - q \equiv 3, 7$. Otherwise $q$ is constant on the cosets of the radical, the quotient form on $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n-1}$ has nondegenerate polar form, and the Gauss sum is twice the quotient's, $\pm 2 \cdot 2^{(n-1)/2}$, with the sign $+$ for $p - q \equiv 1$ and $-$ for $p - q \equiv 5$. The check computes $q$ from the GA squares, the radical, the Gauss sum and the scalar part of $(1 - j)(1 + j)^{p}(1 - j)^{q}$ with $j = e_{1}e_{2}$ in $\Cl(2,0)$ for all $44$ signatures with $1 \le n \le 8$, and compares each with the type of the classification.

\emph{(v)} By Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies} with one plane, the twisted generators $x_{i}\omega$ satisfy the ground relations, $(x_{i}\omega)^{2} = x_{i}^{2}$ because the even element $\omega$ commutes with the ground generators and $\omega^{2} = 1$, and they commute with $e$ and $f$. So the square of the product $y_{A,B}$ of the $x_{i}\omega$, $i \in A$, with $e_{B}$ is $(-1)^{q_{(p,q)}(A)}(-1)^{q_{(1,1)}(B)}$. As $\omega^{|A|}$ is $1$ or $\pm ef$, $y_{A,B}$ is $\pm$ the blade with index set $A \triangle (\{e, f\}$ if $|A|$ is odd$) \triangle B$, which is linear in $(A, B)$ and injective; so it is an isometry $q_{(p,q)} \perp q_{(1,1)} \to q_{(p+1,q+1)}$. The Gauss sum is multiplicative on orthogonal sums, and $q_{(1,1)}$ takes the values $0, 0, 1, 0$ on $\emptyset, \{e\}, \{f\}, \{e,f\}$, Gauss sum $2 = 2^{1}$, Arf invariant $0$; so the sign of the Gauss sum, and with it the type, is unchanged, which is the division-ring clause of Theorem \claimref{tower.rigidity-clock-frozen}. For $(0,2)$, $e_{1}^{2} = e_{2}^{2} = (e_{1}e_{2})^{2} = -1$, Gauss sum $-2$, Arf invariant $1$. The check builds the twisted products in $\Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1)$ for five ground signatures and verifies the squares, the commutation and the bijection. For an anisotropic plane $e', f'$ with $Q(e') = Q(f') = -1$, $\omega' = e'f'$ has $\omega'^{2} = -1$, so $(x_{i}\omega')^{2} = -x_{i}^{2}$: the twisted ground generators have the opposite squares, and the same argument gives an isometry $q_{(q,p)} \perp q_{(0,2)} \to q_{(p,q+2)}$, not $q_{(p,q)} \perp q_{(0,2)}$; so $\Cl(2,2)$, real, comes from $\Cl(2,0)$, real, and $\Cl(0,4)$, quaternionic, from $\Cl(0,2)$, quaternionic. The check verifies this isometry for four ground signatures and the two examples.

check_py:
"""synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form: exact checks.

Blades e_S of Cl(p,q) are indexed by subsets S of the n directions, stored as bitmasks.
q(S) = 1 iff e_S^2 = -1, read from GA products. Everything is exact (Fractions in GA.py).
(1) The sign from symmetry: a skew relation x y = c y x read both ways forces c^2 = 1, and the
    square x^2 commutes with y exactly when c^2 = 1 (normal-ordered model of the quantum plane
    for c = 2, 1/3, -1, 1); in Cl(p,q) the squares of generators are central.
(2) q is a quadratic form over F2 with polar form the anticommutation form, and the closed forms
    q(S) = C(|S|,2) + |S cap Neg| and b(S,T) = |S||T| + |S cap T| (mod 2), for every signature
    with n <= 5; e_S e_T = +/- e_{S xor T} (the vee group is a central extension by +/-1).
(3) Radical, Gauss sum and type, for all 44 signatures with 1 <= n <= 8: the radical is {0} for
    n even and {0, full} for n odd; sum_S (-1)^q(S) = <(1 - j)(1 + j)^p (1 - j)^q>_0 with j a unit
    bivector of a Euclidean plane; its value fixes the type of the classification table.
(4) The (1,1) ascent: the twisted ground blades and the plane blades give an isometry
    q_(p,q) + q_(1,1) -> q_(p+1,q+1); Arf(q_(1,1)) = 0, Arf(q_(0,2)) = 1.
(5) The anisotropic plane: twisting by its volume element (square -1) gives an isometry
    q_(q,p) + q_(0,2) -> q_(p,q+2), not q_(p,q) + q_(0,2); Cl(2,0) -> Cl(2,2) stays real and
    Cl(0,2) -> Cl(0,4) stays quaternionic.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations

import GA
from tp_premise import premise


def blade(mask, n):
    return {tuple(i for i in range(n) if mask >> i & 1): F(1)}


def qform(p, q):
    """q(S) in {0, 1} for every bitmask S, from the GA square of the blade."""
    n = p + q
    S = GA.sig(p, q)
    out = []
    for m in range(2 ** n):
        b = blade(m, n)
        sq = GA.mul(b, b, S)
        assert list(sq) == [()] and sq[()] in (1, -1)
        out.append(0 if sq[()] == 1 else 1)
    return out


def popcount(m):
    return bin(m).count("1")


def gauss(qv):
    return sum(1 - 2 * x for x in qv)


def arf_even(qv, n):
    """Arf invariant of a nondegenerate form on F2^n, n even: the value taken most often."""
    ones = sum(qv)
    if ones == 2 ** (n - 1) - 2 ** (n // 2 - 1):
        return 0
    assert ones == 2 ** (n - 1) + 2 ** (n // 2 - 1)
    return 1


# --- type table of the classification (p - q mod 8) -------------------------
TYPE = {0: "R", 2: "R", 4: "H", 6: "H", 1: "R+R", 5: "H+H", 3: "C", 7: "C"}


def check_symmetry_forces_the_sign():
    premise("std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute")
    # normal-ordered model of k<x,y>/(y x = c^{-1} x y): monomial x^a y^b; y^b x^a = c^(-ab) x^a y^b
    def mono_mul(m1, m2, c):
        (a1, b1), (a2, b2) = m1, m2
        return (c ** (-(b1 * a2)), (a1 + a2, b1 + b2))
    results = {}
    for c in (F(2), F(1, 3), F(-1), F(1)):
        # x y = c y x  <=>  y x = c^{-1} x y ; read with i, j exchanged: y x = c x y, so c^{-1} = c
        symmetric = (c ** -1 == c)
        coef1, m1 = mono_mul((2, 0), (0, 1), c)      # x^2 . y
        coef2, m2 = mono_mul((0, 1), (2, 0), c)      # y . x^2
        assert m1 == m2 == (2, 1)
        central = (coef1 == coef2)
        assert coef1 == c ** 2 * coef2              # x^2 y = c^2 y x^2
        results[c] = (symmetric, central)
    assert all(s == z for s, z in results.values())
    assert [results[c] for c in (F(2), F(-1))] == [(False, False), (True, True)]
    # in Cl(p,q): distinct generators anticommute (c = -1) and every square is central
    for p, q in ((1, 3), (2, 2), (0, 3)):
        S = GA.sig(p, q)
        n = p + q
        for i in range(n):
            sq = GA.mul(GA.gen(i), GA.gen(i), S)
            for j in range(n):
                assert GA.commutes(sq, GA.gen(j), S)
                if i != j:
                    assert GA.anticommutes(GA.gen(i), GA.gen(j), S)
    return True


def check_blade_signs_are_a_quadratic_form():
    premise("std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute")
    count = 0
    for n in range(1, 6):
        for p in range(n + 1):
            q = n - p
            S = GA.sig(p, q)
            qv = qform(p, q)
            neg = sum(1 << i for i in range(p, n))
            for s in range(2 ** n):
                k = popcount(s)
                assert qv[s] == (k * (k - 1) // 2 + popcount(s & neg)) % 2
            for s in range(2 ** n):
                bs = blade(s, n)
                for t in range(2 ** n):
                    bt = blade(t, n)
                    st = GA.mul(bs, bt, S)
                    ts = GA.mul(bt, bs, S)
                    # e_S e_T = +/- e_{S xor T}
                    assert list(st) == list(blade(s ^ t, n)) and abs(st[tuple(st)[0]]) == 1
                    anti = 1 if GA.eq(st, GA.neg(ts)) else 0
                    assert anti == (0 if GA.eq(st, ts) else 1)
                    polar = (qv[s ^ t] + qv[s] + qv[t]) % 2
                    assert polar == anti
                    assert anti == (popcount(s) * popcount(t) + popcount(s & t)) % 2
            count += 1
    assert count == 20
    return True


def check_radical_gauss_sum_and_type():
    premise("transport.classification-real-clifford-algebras")
    premise("primer.sign")
    E2 = GA.sig(2, 0)
    j = {(0, 1): F(1)}
    one = GA.sc(1)
    assert GA.eq(GA.mul(j, j, E2), GA.sc(-1))
    seen = {}
    for n in range(1, 9):
        full = 2 ** n - 1
        for p in range(n + 1):
            q = n - p
            qv = qform(p, q)
            pol = lambda s, t: (popcount(s) * popcount(t) + popcount(s & t)) % 2
            gens = [1 << i for i in range(n)]
            radical = [s for s in range(2 ** n) if all(pol(s, g) == 0 for g in gens)]
            g = gauss(qv)
            # the Gauss sum in the algebra: <(1 - j)(1 + j)^p (1 - j)^q>_0
            x = GA.sub(one, j)
            for _ in range(p):
                x = GA.mul(x, GA.add(one, j), E2)
            for _ in range(q):
                x = GA.mul(x, GA.sub(one, j), E2)
            assert x.get((), F(0)) == g
            t = TYPE[(p - q) % 8]
            if n % 2 == 0:
                assert radical == [0]
                assert g * g == 2 ** n
                arf = arf_even(qv, n)
                assert (arf == 0) == (t == "R") and (arf == 1) == (t == "H")
                assert g == (2 ** (n // 2)) * (1 - 2 * arf)
            else:
                assert radical == [0, full]
                omega_sq_neg = qv[full]
                assert (omega_sq_neg == 1) == (t == "C")
                if omega_sq_neg:
                    assert g == 0
                else:
                    assert g * g == 2 ** (n + 1)
                    split = 0 if g > 0 else 1
                    assert (split == 0) == (t == "R+R") and (split == 1) == (t == "H+H")
            seen[(p, q)] = t
    assert len(seen) == 44
    assert sum(1 for (p, q) in seen if (p + q) % 2 == 0) == 24
    return True


def check_ascent_adds_a_hyperbolic_plane():
    premise("tower.commuting-copies")
    premise("tower.rigidity-clock-frozen")
    qH = qform(1, 1)
    q02 = qform(0, 2)
    assert arf_even(qH, 2) == 0 and arf_even(q02, 2) == 1
    assert q02 == [0, 1, 1, 1]
    for p, q in ((1, 3), (0, 2), (2, 1), (1, 1), (0, 3)):
        n = p + q
        # Cl(p+1, q+1): ground generators 0..n-1 reordered to keep the signature layout:
        # positive ground 0..p-1, e = p, negative ground p+1..p+q, f = n+1
        S = GA.sig(p + 1, q + 1)
        ground = list(range(p)) + list(range(p + 1, p + 1 + q))
        e, f = p, n + 1
        omega = GA.mul(GA.gen(e), GA.gen(f), S)
        assert GA.eq(GA.mul(omega, omega, S), GA.sc(1))
        twisted = [GA.mul(GA.gen(g), omega, S) for g in ground]
        plane = [GA.gen(e), GA.gen(f)]
        qg = qform(p, q)
        images = set()
        for A in range(2 ** n):
            xa = GA.sc(1)
            for i in range(n):
                if A >> i & 1:
                    xa = GA.mul(xa, twisted[i], S)
            for B in range(4):
                y = xa
                for i in range(2):
                    if B >> i & 1:
                        y = GA.mul(y, plane[i], S)
                assert len(y) == 1
                (bl, c), = y.items()
                images.add(bl)
                sq = GA.mul(y, y, S)
                assert sq == {(): F(1 - 2 * ((qg[A] + qH[B]) % 2))}
                for g in twisted:
                    for h in plane:
                        assert GA.commutes(g, h, S)
        assert len(images) == 2 ** (n + 2)
    return True


def check_anisotropic_plane_exchanges_p_and_q():
    premise("tower.commuting-copies")
    q02 = qform(0, 2)
    for p, q in ((2, 0), (0, 2), (1, 3), (1, 2)):
        n = p + q
        # Cl(p, q+2): positive ground 0..p-1, negative ground p..p+q-1, plane e' = n, f' = n+1
        S = GA.sig(p, q + 2)
        ground = list(range(n))
        e, f = n, n + 1
        omega = GA.mul(GA.gen(e), GA.gen(f), S)
        assert GA.eq(GA.mul(omega, omega, S), GA.sc(-1))
        twisted = [GA.mul(GA.gen(g), omega, S) for g in ground]
        plane = [GA.gen(e), GA.gen(f)]
        # the twisted generators have the opposite squares: signature (q, p), listed as such
        for i, g in enumerate(twisted):
            assert GA.mul(g, g, S) == {(): F(-1 if i < p else 1)}
            for h in plane:
                assert GA.commutes(g, h, S)
        qrev = qform(q, p)
        # ground index i < p is a negative direction of the twisted (q, p) form: reorder masks
        perm = list(range(p, n)) + list(range(p))      # twisted index i sits at position perm.index(i)
        images = set()
        for A in range(2 ** n):
            Arev = sum(1 << perm.index(i) for i in range(n) if A >> i & 1)
            xa = GA.sc(1)
            for i in range(n):
                if A >> i & 1:
                    xa = GA.mul(xa, twisted[i], S)
            for B in range(4):
                y = xa
                for i in range(2):
                    if B >> i & 1:
                        y = GA.mul(y, plane[i], S)
                assert len(y) == 1
                images.add(list(y)[0])
                assert GA.mul(y, y, S) == {(): F(1 - 2 * ((qrev[Arev] + q02[B]) % 2))}
        assert len(images) == 2 ** (n + 2)
    # the two examples: Arf(q_(2,2)) = Arf(q_(0,2)) + Arf(q_(0,2)) = 0 = Arf(q_(2,0)); Cl(0,4) has Arf 1
    assert arf_even(qform(2, 2), 4) == 0 == arf_even(qform(2, 0), 2)
    assert (arf_even(q02, 2) + arf_even(q02, 2)) % 2 == 0
    assert arf_even(qform(0, 4), 4) == 1 == arf_even(q02, 2)
    assert (arf_even(qform(2, 0), 2) + 1) % 2 != arf_even(qform(2, 2), 4)
    return True
